A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EoS-FM research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and included supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pangaea evaluations, ensemble-size and normalization ablations, and supplementary repeated-run experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original downstream evaluations, computational-efficiency measurements, scaling experiments, and analyses comparing learned and manually curated encoder subsets.

M1.justification: v3 replaces multiple index-based band mappings with one prioritized, wavelength-aware mapping per encoder, including band expressions and cross-modality fallback. It also replaces v1's hard top-k selection procedure with a top-k-tail L1 training penalty and hard selection during validation/inference. These change input adaptation and optimization; feature normalization and linear fusion remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds the CV4A Kenya Crop Type training dataset and its Sentinel-2 multitemporal segmentation specialist, expanding reported training coverage from 16 to 17 datasets. The same 11 downstream Pangaea tasks remain; extending analyses to previously evaluated tasks does not add benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Tables 2–3, v3 Tables 1–2 add TerraMind and Thor: Large variants for full-data comparisons and Base variants for 10% supervision. These introduce substantial recent competitors, including TerraMind's near-leading reported aggregate result. The original Pangaea comparison methods and supervised baselines remain.

E3.justification: The full model configuration changes from 21 encoders/72M parameters to 22/76M. v3 introduces fixed-hardware GFLOPs/FPS evaluation, controlled learned-versus-curated encoder comparisons, and nine-task DTB aggregation for TerraMind/Thor alongside eleven-task averages for other models. The retained downstream protocol still specifies 80 epochs and batch size 8; newly disclosed implementation settings do not establish additional protocol changes.

E4.justification: v3 extends ensemble-size analysis from HLS Burn Scars to include AI4SmallFarms, revises the HLS scaling results, and adds encoder-selection frequencies, modality-coherence analysis, and learned-versus-curated subset ablations on AI4SmallFarms and MADOS. The dedicated v1 stability analysis disappears. The normalization ablation in Table 4 remains unchanged.

E5.justification: v1's supplement provides individual runs and mean/standard deviation for ten tasks, excluding BioMassters. v3 removes these statistics and instead states that Table 1 averages three random-seed evaluations per dataset, without reporting dispersion. Repeated-run evaluation therefore was not newly introduced. v3 also adds Pearson correlation and trend estimation with PASTIS excluded.

E6.justification: Many full and Small model results change. Full-data HLS is 81.92 in v1's main table, 80.73 in its supplementary three-run average, and 87.01 in v3; Small-model PASTIS changes from 27.45 to 19.35. v3 adds efficiency and encoder-selection results. These concern revised model/reporting conditions; changed DTB values also reflect the expanded comparison pool, not simply performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3.3 introduces the formal top-k-tail L1 objective, its equivalent total-L1-minus-top-k expression, and an almost-everywhere differentiability argument. Appendix D additionally defines the modality-coherence score. These are bounded additions to mathematical definitions and reasoning, without a substantial theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The abstract, four listed contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: independently trained specialists can form an efficient generalist representation, with learned selection, pruning, modular extension, and federated applicability. The new representation-level framing elaborates this existing contribution rather than redefining its scope.

C2.justification: v3 changes the scaling interpretation from emphasizing nonmonotonic selection weaknesses to task-dependent saturation and pruning benefits. It adds explanations involving reduced overfitting, hardware overhead, and unexpectedly useful or potentially ignored modality-mismatched encoders. Appendix E also discloses convergence-related loss exceptions and argues that their effect on baseline comparability is negligible.

D1.justification: v3 adds code/pretrained-model access information and extensive training/evaluation documentation: specialist heads, optimizer, precision, per-dataset epochs and times, a reported 79.38-hour H100 budget, temporal aggregation, decoder dimensions, native-resolution handling, learning-rate schedule, and loss exceptions. These substantially improve documented reproducibility; details absent from v1 do not alone demonstrate implementation changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds substantive positioning against Panopticon, SMARTIES, and Copernicus-FM, distinguishing independently trained specialists from unified adaptive backbones. It also relates pruning to MAPEX and sharpens the distinction from task-specific ensembling. TerraMind, Thor, Kenya Crop Type, and temporal-attention references are added, while the Taskonomy citation disappears.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites and condenses parts of the introduction and discussion, expands related-work explanations, and revises the method and results narrative. Feature-normalization exposition moves into Appendix B, and the numbered stability-focused supplement is reorganized into lettered sections on normalization, training, encoder selection, and testing.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the architecture and scaling figures, adds efficiency/training-budget tables and selection/modality plots, removes the stability tables, and relocates the retained feature-variance figure to the appendix. The supplement changes from one-column to two-column layout. Figure 1 also drops the HLS radar axis despite retaining an eleven-task caption.

improvement.justification: The efficiency measurements, training budgets, detailed protocols, stronger comparison methods, and encoder-selection controls make v3's central claims better supported and its experiments easier to reproduce. The net gain is limited by removing v1's run-level uncertainty reporting and comparing headline DTB averages over different task sets. These weaknesses prevent the expanded evidence from establishing a substantial overall improvement.
